Acute Bronchitis.description: Inflammation of the bronchial airways commonly following a viral respiratory illness, causing cough, mucus, and chest tightness.
precautions: Rest adequately and avoid cold drafts
Drink warm fluids and herbal teas
Use warm saline steam inhalation twice daily
Avoid exposure to cigarette smoke and atmospheric pollutants
Consult a physician if cough persists beyond 10 days

Pneumonia.description: Acute infection of the lung parenchyma causing alveolar fluid accumulation, characterized by high fever, severe chills, persistent productive cough, and breathing difficulty.
precautions: Seek immediate clinical evaluation with chest X-ray
Monitor blood oxygen saturation with pulse oximeter
Maintain strict oral hydration with electrolytes
Complete any doctor-prescribed antimicrobial regimen
Do not delay seeking emergency care if breathlessness worsens

Common Cold.description: Mild, self-limiting viral infection of the nasal mucosa and upper respiratory tract causing congestion, sneezing, and runny nose.
precautions: Get plenty of rest and sleep
Gargle with warm salt water for throat relief
Stay hydrated with warm water, broths, and soups
Practice frequent hand washing to prevent transmission
Use saline nasal drops for nasal congestion

Malaria.description: Mosquito-borne parasitic infection characterized by paroxysmal high fever cycles, shaking chills, profuse sweating, and generalized aches.
precautions: Obtain immediate peripheral blood smear / rapid antigen test
Take antimalarial medications strictly under medical prescription
Use mosquito repellent and bed nets consistently
Maintain high fluid and electrolyte intake
Rest completely until fever resolves

Dengue Fever.description: Acute mosquito-borne arboviral illness causing sudden onset high fever, intense retro-orbital headache, severe joint/muscle pain, and characteristic skin rash.
precautions: Monitor platelet counts daily under medical supervision
Avoid aspirin and NSAIDs due to bleeding risks
Maintain aggressive oral hydration with ORS and fresh fluids
Watch for warning signs like persistent vomiting or bleeding
Rest in mosquito-screened quarters

Typhoid Fever.description: Systemic bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, presenting with prolonged stepwise fever, abdominal discomfort, headache, and bowel irregularities.
precautions: Consume only boiled or purified drinking water
Eat easily digestible, freshly cooked bland meals
Complete full course of antibiotics prescribed by physician
Practice rigorous hand hygiene before handling food
Consult physician for blood culture or serological testing

Gastroenteritis (Food Poisoning).description: Acute inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract caused by foodborne bacteria, viruses, or toxins, resulting in watery diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal cramps.
precautions: Sip Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) continuously to prevent dehydration
Follow a gentle diet (bananas, rice, applesauce, toast)
Avoid dairy products, caffeine, alcohol, and oily foods
Wash hands thoroughly with soap before food preparation
Seek medical care if vomiting persists or blood appears in stools

Acid Reflux (GERD).description: Digestive disease where stomach acid repeatedly flows back into the food pipe, irritating the esophageal lining and causing heartburn and upper abdominal discomfort.
precautions: Avoid lying down within 3 hours after eating meals
Elevate head of bed by 6 inches during sleep
Limit acidic, spicy, fried foods, caffeine, and chocolate
Eat smaller, more frequent meals rather than large dinners
Maintain healthy weight and avoid tight-fitting garments

Hypertension (High BP).description: Long-term cardiovascular condition where systemic arterial pressure is chronically elevated, often presenting with morning headaches, dizziness, and fatigue.
precautions: Restrict daily dietary sodium (salt) intake
Engage in 30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise daily
Avoid smoking, alcohol, and excessive psychological stress
Record blood pressure readings twice daily in a home log
Take prescribed antihypertensive medications consistently

Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.description: Chronic metabolic disorder marked by persistent hyperglycemia resulting from progressive insulin resistance and impaired insulin secretion.
precautions: Monitor fasting and post-meal blood glucose regularly
Strictly limit refined carbohydrates, sugars, and sweetened beverages
Incorporate daily physical activity to improve insulin sensitivity
Inspect feet daily for unnoticed cuts, blisters, or sores
Schedule regular HbA1c, renal, and retinal checkups

Jaundice (Hepatitis).description: Clinical manifestation of liver dysfunction characterized by hyperbilirubinemia, leading to yellowish discoloration of skin and eyes, dark urine, and fatigue.
precautions: Undergo Liver Function Tests (LFT) and viral hepatitis screening
Strictly abstain from all alcoholic beverages and hepatotoxic drugs
Consume a clean, low-fat, nutrient-dense diet with ample boiled water
Ensure complete bed rest during the acute symptomatic phase
Avoid unpurified water and roadside food vendors

Migraine.description: Primary headache disorder marked by recurrent moderate-to-severe throbbing unilateral head pain, commonly accompanied by sensory sensitivity, nausea, and dizziness.
precautions: Rest in a dark, quiet, temperature-controlled room during attacks
Identify and avoid individual triggers like caffeine or sensory overload
Apply a cold compress to the forehead or neck
Stay consistently hydrated throughout the day
Maintain regular sleep and meal schedules

Osteoarthritis.description: Degenerative joint disease resulting from progressive breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone, causing chronic pain, stiffness, and reduced mobility.
precautions: Engage in low-impact joint-friendly exercises like swimming or walking
Maintain optimal body weight to reduce joint load bearing
Use warm compresses for stiffness and cold packs for swelling
Use supportive walking aids or braces when recommended
Avoid prolonged static standing or high-impact activities

Allergic Rhinitis.description: Allergic inflammatory condition of the nasal mucous membranes triggered by environmental allergens like pollen, dust mites, or animal dander.
precautions: Minimize exposure to known environmental allergens and pollen
Keep windows closed during peak pollen count hours
Use HEPA air purifiers in sleeping quarters
Perform regular saline nasal rinses
Wash bedding frequently in hot water to eliminate dust mites

Urinary Tract Infection (UTI).description: Bacterial infection affecting the urinary tract, commonly presenting with burning urination, urinary frequency, and lower abdominal discomfort.
precautions: Drink plenty of water (2.5 - 3 liters daily) to flush urinary passages
Urinate promptly when the urge arises without holding
Consult a physician for urine routine and culture sensitivity testing
Complete full course of antibiotics if prescribed by doctor
Avoid harsh feminine hygiene sprays or scented soaps

Asthma.description: Chronic inflammatory airway disorder characterized by episodic airway hyperresponsiveness, causing wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and coughing.
precautions: Keep physician-prescribed rescue inhaler accessible at all times
Identify and avoid personal triggers (dust, cold air, smoke, pollen)
Monitor peak expiratory flow if instructed by your doctor
Take daily preventative controller medications as prescribed
Seek immediate emergency care if breathing distress fails to respond to inhaler
